Paper briefing

DeltaVLM
and ChangeChat-105k

Interactive Remote Sensing Image Change Analysis via Instruction-Guided Difference Perception

Pei Deng, Wenqian Zhou, Hanlin Wu

Remote Sensing 2026, 18(4), 541
arXiv v1: July 2025

A benchmark of general chat VLMs accompanies a trained model. Its spatial task uses a nine-cell grid.

ChangeChat-105k benchmarkDeltaVLM model

The paper contains direct general-model evaluation. The proposed method itself receives task-specific training.

arXiv v1, table I · Released annotation dataset
Annotation pipeline

Existing captions and masks supply the supervision

  1. LEVIR-CC provides paired imagery and human-written change descriptions.
  2. LEVIR-MCI supplies pixel-level maps for change labels, counts, and grid locations.
  3. Contour extraction supplies category counts and spatial information.
  4. ChatGPT expands captions and structured information into open-ended questions and responses.

For open-ended generation, the paper says ChatGPT receives captions, contours, and counts without the images. These are generated reference answers rather than a new human census of every visible change.

Spatial output

Localization is a nine-cell classification task

LeftCenterRight
TLTCTR
CLCCCR
BLBCBR

Top, center, and bottom rows

The annotation divides a change map into nine cells.

A cell qualifies when more than 5% of its pixels changed.

The model returns the qualifying cells for roads or buildings.

A correct grid answer can still have inaccurate object boundaries. Grid F1 and Jaccard similarity do not measure pixel-mask overlap.

Architecture

An instruction selects visual difference features

A shared visual encoder extracts both dates. The difference module filters contextual features. An instruction-guided Q-former compresses them into tokens for the language decoder.

Original paper figure 4 and section IV
Training

The language decoder stays frozen

ComponentTraining role
EVA-ViT-g/14 visual encoderThe paper fine-tunes its final two blocks and freezes the first 37
Cross-semantic relation measuringLearns gates that filter contextual difference features
Instruction-guided Q-formerLearns 32 query embeddings and cross-modal alignment
Vicuna-7B language decoderRemains frozen while visual and alignment modules adapt

The objective supervises generated response tokens. A frozen language decoder does not make the complete DeltaVLM system training-free.

Paper sections IV-B to IV-E · Official model summary
General chat-model evaluation

The comparison includes image-input general VLMs

Source versionGeneral-model baselines
arXiv v1GPT-4o, Qwen-VL-Plus, GLM-4V-Plus, Gemini-1.5-Pro
Published 2026 articleAdds DeepSeek-VL2, alongside the four general models
Specialized comparisonsRS captioning models and, in the published version, RSUniVLM

The general models answer the benchmark’s image-pair questions. DeltaVLM uses the same task categories after supervised adaptation.

Baseline names describe the authors’ reported runs. The accessible descriptions do not supply a full audit of provider snapshots or prompt-search budgets.

Published article, table 5 · Spatial response definition
Language outputs

Captioning and open QA use text-reference metrics

Captioning

BLEU, METEOR, ROUGE-L, and CIDEr compare generated descriptions with reference text.

LEVIR-CC provides multiple reference captions for an image pair.

Open-ended QA

Published table 6 reports CIDEr of 203.34 for DeltaVLM and 170.08 for DeepSeek-VL2.

A score on generated reference wording is not a direct pixel- or event-level correctness measure.

Results change between arXiv v1 and the published article. Keep a single version’s table intact when reproducing a comparison.

Published article, tables 2 and 6 · Metric definitions, arXiv v1
Relation to dense change evaluation

The benchmark leaves finer spatial and relational questions open

What ChangeChat-105k evaluatesA different evaluation can test
Whether an image pair changedWhether a particular source-to-destination transition occurred
Road/building counts and 3×3 locationsQuery-specific boxes or masks with foreground spatial metrics
Task-specific questions and contextual dialogueMatched temporal relations on identical candidate regions
General-model baselines under reported promptsValidation-selected prompts and their held-out transfer

These differences describe evaluation scope. They do not establish novelty against all related literature or guarantee a publication contribution.
